items.title: XPENG Details Mass-Production IRON Humanoid at AI Day 2026, Confirms Unisex Form Factor and VLA 3.0
items.summary: XPENG debuted the mass-production iteration of the IRON humanoid robot at AI Day 2026, confirming a standardized unisex form factor for deployment. The robot utilizes XPENG's Turing Physical AI Architecture (VLA 3.0) across three AI chips to achieve 76 degrees of freedom and extensive tactile sensing. Hardware mass production is scheduled to start in January 2027 on an automated line, targeting a Q2 2027 commercial launch. IRON features advanced safety systems, including collision mitigation and a solid-state battery capable of 200-degree Celsius tolerance. The company plans to offer IRON as a configurable "work partner" through skill packs and subscription plans post-delivery.
items.audio_script: From Humanoids Daily, XPENG Details Mass-Production IRON Humanoid at AI Day 2026, Confirms Unisex Form Factor and VLA 3.0. This report details the unveiling of the mass-production iteration of the IRON humanoid robot, confirming a standardized unisex form factor and the utilization of the Turing Physical AI Architecture version three point zero. The robot employs XPENG's architecture across three AI chips to achieve seventy-six degrees of freedom and comprehensive tactile sensing. Hardware mass production is slated to commence in January two thousand twenty-seven on an automated line, with a commercial launch targeted for the second quarter of two thousand twenty-seven. The IRON model incorporates advanced safety mechanisms, including collision mitigation protocols and a solid-state battery capable of withstanding two hundred degrees Celsius. The company intends to deliver the IRON as a configurable work partner via skill packs and subscription plans following delivery. This development signals a tangible progression toward deployable, standardized humanoid robotics within the near future.

items.title: Volvo Cars begins training Hexagon humanoid robots for factory work
items.summary: Volvo Cars is training Hexagon AEON humanoid robots at its Ghent plant to integrate them into production by mid-2027. This facility is the first Volvo plant to trial these robots, training them to perform tasks alongside human workers and existing automation. The training utilizes imitation learning, starting with precise component placement and progressing to more complex activities. Humanoid robots are being explored for their mobility and ability to work in existing factory environments. This initiative aims to improve safety, flexibility, and operational efficiency in automotive manufacturing.

This development signals a tangible step in deploying advanced robotics within complex industrial environments.

items.title: Universal Robots brings Inbolt’s 3D AI vision directly onto its Gen 7 robots
items.summary: Universal Robots and Inbolt integrated AI-powered 3D vision guidance directly into the Universal Robots Gen 7 robots. This allows the robots to identify components and adjust trajectories based on their real-time positions during production. The Inbolt Standard software runs natively on the robot's controller, eliminating the need for separate computing hardware. This integration reduces the need for customized jigs and fixtures when handling new products, simplifying robotic vision. The system supports various industrial applications and allows for quick training on new components from CAD files.

items.title: FCC should focus on robot security, not country of origin
items.summary: The FCC should focus robot security on the software controlling the devices rather than their country of origin. The actual security boundary lies in the code, data, and control mechanisms, not the physical chassis. Regulated systems must demonstrate secure code updates, data handling, and access controls. This necessitates standards for provenance of control, vulnerability patching, and independent safety layers for AI. Ultimately, regulation should focus on who controls the code and how remote access is managed.
items.audio_script: From The Robot Report, "FCC should focus on robot security, not country of origin". This segment addresses the prioritization of regulatory focus for robot security, asserting that the security boundary resides in the software and control mechanisms rather than the physical origin of the hardware. The report indicates that regulated systems require standards concerning secure code updates, data handling protocols, and access controls. This focus necessitates establishing standards for the provenance of control, vulnerability patching procedures, and independent safety layers for artificial intelligence systems. Ultimately, the report concludes that regulation must concentrate on the entity controlling the code and the methods used for managing remote access. The technology sector must address these software-centric security requirements immediately to establish effective regulatory frameworks.

items.title: How DARPA Challenged Teams to Bring Robots Into Disaster Triage
items.summary: DARPA recently organized a grand challenge to demonstrate the life-saving potential of robots in emergency triage situations. The challenge aimed to prove that robots could effectively assist in disaster scenarios. Teams competed to develop and deploy robotic solutions for these critical tasks. During the finals, a Spot robot from the University of Maryland’s RoboScout team was shown surveying the area. This event highlighted the practical application of robotics in disaster response.

items.title: When robots lose contact: Research examines the resilience of decentralized robot swarms
items.summary: Research investigated the resilience of decentralized robot swarms when communication is lost, finding that disconnected robots can still perform useful work based on their local memory. A study simulating pressure vessel inspection compared decentralized methods, like M-PSO, against leader-based approaches in extreme conditions. Decentralized coordination achieved a higher success rate in local location estimation compared to leader-based methods. However, the research also showed that while decentralized systems can store information locally, communication failures prevent easy retrieval of that information. The findings suggest decentralized intelligence is valuable for preserving data, but additional engineering is needed for reliable information transmission.

The research involved a simulation comparing decentralized methods, such as M-PSO, against leader-based approaches during pressure vessel inspection under extreme conditions. Decentralized coordination demonstrated a higher success rate in local location estimation compared to leader-based methods. However, the study also indicated that while decentralized systems maintain local information, communication failures impede the easy retrieval of that stored data. This suggests that decentralized intelligence is beneficial for data preservation, but requires further engineering for reliable information transmission in complex systems. The findings point toward the importance of developing robust communication protocols for future autonomous swarm applications.

items.title: Heavy metal acrobatics: Researchers teach five-ton construction vehicle to balance on two wheels
items.summary: Researchers used reinforcement learning to train an AI to enable a five-ton skid-steer loader to balance and perform complex maneuvers on two wheels. This involved collecting operational data to develop a neural network predicting actuator behavior for autonomous control. The AI system successfully demonstrated stationary balancing, in-place spinning, and navigating terrain with undulations up to 75 cm. The reinforcement learning approach proved more capable in certain demanding maneuvers compared to a conventional model predictive control system. This research suggests a foundation for future autonomous control of heavy machinery in various industries.

items.title: KIRO plans KAREX-M humanoid for Antarctic heavy lifting
items.summary: KIRO is developing KAREX-M, a hybrid mobile humanoid for installing and maintaining observation infrastructure in Antarctica. The project has 6 billion won in funding and aims to develop two integrated platforms for Antarctic missions around 2030. KAREX-M features a wheel/track base and a hydraulic dual-arm upper body designed for heavy lifting and manipulation. It will utilize a battery/generator hybrid system for up to 200 km travel and incorporate AI for route planning and remote operation. The plan involves staged testing and targets deploying the robots for infrastructure construction in Antarctica by 2030.

items.title: Exotec helps Fnac Darty handle Black Friday rush with refurbished and rented robots
items.summary: Fnac Darty partnered with Exotec to automate its Massy logistics facility using refurbished robots for the Black Friday rush. The system includes 36 robots and storage locations to increase order processing capacity. During peak demand, the retailer can rent additional robots to temporarily double its throughput. Much of the automation equipment was refurbished from a previous operation, demonstrating equipment reuse. This modular approach allows retailers to increase capacity flexibly without major upfront investment.

items.title: AutomationML to join OPC Foundation to strengthen industrial interoperability
items.summary: AutomationML and the OPC Foundation plan to combine their technologies and communities, with AutomationML joining the OPC Foundation by January 1, 2027. This integration will transfer AutomationML's technology to the OPC Foundation to create a unified framework for industrial interoperability. The goal is to establish a consistent method for exchanging engineering and operational information across automation systems, supporting digital twins and AI. This unification aims to preserve the meaning of information throughout the entire industrial lifecycle, from engineering to decommissioning. The merger seeks to reduce silos between engineering and operational data to facilitate better interoperability and value creation.

items.title: The next generation of bionic hands is here—and they can feel
items.source: MIT Technology Review - AI & Emerging Tech
items.summary: An experimental bionic hand, wired to nerves in the forearm, allows a patient to feel pressure for the first time. Avi Davidson, a participant in a University of Utah clinical trial, is the first to use this device independently. The research focuses on connecting the prosthetic to the nervous system to enable both movement control and sensory feedback. The process involved surgically implanting electrodes into nerves and training a computer system to translate nerve signals into hand movements and sensations. Despite functional improvements, Davidson experiences phantom pain and wrist strain, prompting further research into the technology's long-term effects.
items.audio_script: From MIT Technology Review - AI & Emerging Tech, "The next generation of bionic hands is here—and they can feel". This report details the development of an experimental bionic hand capable of providing sensory feedback to the user. The research involved connecting a prosthetic hand to the nerves in the forearm to enable the perception of pressure. A participant in a University of Utah clinical trial, Avi Davidson, was the first to use this device independently, which required surgically implanting electrodes into nerves and training a computer system to translate nerve signals into both movement control and sensation. Despite functional improvements, Davidson reported experiences of phantom pain and wrist strain, which directs ongoing research into the technology's long-term implications. This advancement signals further progress in interfacing artificial systems with the human nervous system.

items.title: Designing Robot Gripper Fingers for Repeatable Changeovers
items.summary: Repeatable changeovers require designing the finger interface to ensure consistent workpiece positioning across different installations. This involves tracing requirements from the receiving operation back through the tooling to define necessary geometric relationships and acceptance criteria. Locating features must be defined separately from fasteners, and reference surfaces should be accessible for inspection. A clear spare-parts policy and rigorous post-change testing are crucial to ensure predictable maintenance. Ultimately, a replacement should restore a known arrangement with documented evidence that it meets process requirements.

Locating features must be defined independently from fasteners, and reference surfaces require accessibility for inspection. A spare-parts policy and rigorous post-change testing are identified as crucial elements for predictable maintenance. Ultimately, a replacement must restore a known arrangement with documented evidence confirming adherence to process requirements. This work establishes a framework for manufacturing highly adaptable robotic end-effectors. The industry should focus on developing standardized interfaces for machine tooling.

items.title: Space robotics: notes from an IROS 2026 plenary session
items.summary: Speakers from NASA, JAXA, and academia discussed the role of robots in lunar exploration, human spaceflight, and orbital work. Potential applications include unloading cargo, building lunar infrastructure, and space debris removal. Investment in lunar robotics can advance terrestrial industries like construction, logistics, and mining by sharing relevant challenges. NASA is shifting focus to MoonBase, requiring robotic systems for habitat construction, resource utilization, and in-situ resource utilization. Autonomous robotics is also critical for future deep-space missions requiring less human intervention.

items.title: Physical AI model outpaces human operator in robot manipulation tests
items.summary: A physical AI model named FLUX-mimic-x outperformed a human operator in speed for everyday robotic manipulation tasks. It completed tasks in a median of 11 seconds, compared to 27 seconds for the human. Another model, Praxis-1, showed the ability to recover from mistakes during task execution. The most reliable dedicated robot models on the leaderboard utilize video models rather than conventional vision-language models. These results suggest a shift towards world-action models in the robotics industry.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, Physical AI model outpaces human operator in robot manipulation tests. This report details performance benchmarks where an AI model demonstrated superior speed in executing everyday robotic manipulation tasks compared to a human operator. The study involved testing several physical AI models against human performance in manipulation scenarios. The FLUX-mimic-x model achieved a median completion time of eleven seconds for these tasks, contrasting with a median time of twenty-seven seconds recorded for the human participant. Furthermore, another model named Praxis-1 exhibited the capability to recover from errors during the task execution process. The research indicates that the most reliable dedicated robot models on the leaderboard are utilizing video models instead of traditional vision-language models, suggesting a significant shift toward world-action models within the robotics industry. This development points toward increased expectations for autonomous, real-world action capabilities in future robotic systems.

items.title: Effect-Driven Skill Abstractions for Offline Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: The research proposes learning discrete skill abstractions to aid long-horizon, goal-conditioned reinforcement learning. It argues that goal-directed skills should be based on how they affect the agent's state rather than simple action quantization. A novel method optimizes action chunk predictions conditioned on the current state and action to ensure skills are distinguished by the resulting future states. This framework can be integrated with offline RL by replacing continuous action heads with discrete skill selection mechanisms. Experiments on navigation and manipulation tasks demonstrate significant performance improvements over existing baselines.

items.title: Why Does Sensor Depth Fail Learned Manipulation Policies? Finding the Failure Mode with ACT
items.summary: Learned manipulation policies primarily rely on RGB images, though depth data can offer performance gains. Depth cameras introduce both measurement noise and missing depth values, the effects of which are not fully understood. Calibration showed that complete depth improves success by about ten percentage points, with gains persisting even with significant noise. However, holes covering one-sixth of the image eliminated the benefit of depth, and reliance on depth masks heavily influences performance. Consequently, depth camera utility for learned policies should be assessed based on depth coverage rather than just measurement precision.

items.title: FOCI: Trajectory Optimization on Gaussian Splats for Gaussian Robots
items.summary: FOCI proposes an algorithm to optimize trajectories directly on 3D Gaussian Splats for Gaussian robots. It utilizes a novel collision formulation based on the overlap integral between Gaussians to assess traversability. This method represents both the environment and the robot as Gaussian Splats, allowing for orientation-aware planning through narrow spaces. Testing shows that collision-free trajectories for various robot types can be computed quickly, even with numerous Gaussians. The approach offers an advantage over bounding box methods by providing a more accurate representation of traversability.

items.title: RoboARC: Physical Puzzles for Robotic Manipulation under Spatial Constraints
items.summary: RoboARC introduces a benchmark of 90 physical puzzles involving spatial constraints for robotic manipulation with rigid and soft materials. The tasks are defined by frozen scenes with physics-based grading and verified reference solutions. Agents, including coding agents and Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies, are evaluated on solving these tasks under privileged (full state access) and standard (real-sensor input) regimes. GPT-6 Astra proved the strongest, solving 86% of the tasks in the privileged regime, while most other tested agents struggled significantly. The work investigates whether robots can reason out necessary motions when manipulation is governed by precise spatial constraints.

items.title: An Adversarial Multi-Agent Pursuit Game for Locomotor Agility Pretraining
items.summary: Agile humanoid locomotion requires controllers that can adapt to changing motion demands while maintaining stability. The research explores using an adversarial multi-agent pursuit game to pretrain locomotion agility. The method involves training neural networks in a physics simulator to learn new motion generation and control strategies through competitive self-play. A task suite called MJTag is presented for role-conditioned locomotion during competitive pursuit-evasion. This setup allows the locomotion controller to adopt skills like dodging and sprinting via sparse feedback and adversarial training.

items.title: OnCue: Generating Safety-Critical Driving Scenarios under Occlusion with Temporal Control
items.summary: OnCue is a framework designed to generate safety-critical driving scenarios under occlusion by incorporating temporal control. It uses scene geometry to create hidden starts and timed waypoints for pedestrian, cyclist, and vehicle trajectories. The method employs an offline response oracle to label encounters as Reactive or Anticipatory and store safe maneuvers as demonstrations. Results show that temporal control significantly impacts collision risk and planner performance under occlusion. This research emphasizes the value of temporal control for evaluating and improving autonomous driving planners.

items.title: Model Predictive Control of a Multirotor UAV with a Cable-Suspended Payload: A Comparison of Shifted and Transformer-Based Warm Starts
items.summary: The study compares model predictive control (MPC) for a multirotor UAV with a cable-suspended payload using different warm-starting techniques. It investigates the use of conventional shifted initialization versus Transformer-based warm starting for a sequential convex programming optimizer. Numerical experiments show that Transformer initialization reduces computation time for independently solved MPC problems. However, shifting the previous control sequence yields the fastest time in sequential closed-loop simulations. All methods resulted in similar tracking behavior during simulation.

items.title: Skeptic: Grounding Failure Diagnosis for Robot Skill Discovery
items.summary: Robot agents can fail in skill discovery when they incorrectly judge a program's failure as physical impossibility. Skeptic is introduced as a training-free protocol to diagnose this grounding failure using measured action outcomes and task success. The method employs a grounded event log to separate sensor observations from inferred diagnoses of action effects. Verified promotion incorporates a development-success requirement to check for independent reproduction of the source program. This approach reduced false impossibility judgments across audited tasks and improved held-out success rates.

items.title: DexEngine: Scaling Human Demonstrations into Physically Executable Whole-Robot Data
items.summary: DexEngine is a simulation pipeline designed to transform human hand-object demonstrations into physically executable whole-robot data. It achieves this by positioning demonstrations, finding arm motions that follow the human actions, and correcting these motions using physics simulation and residual reinforcement learning. The method generates a large dataset from human data to train whole-robot policies. Policies trained with this data significantly outperform those without physics correction, demonstrating the necessity of incorporating physical constraints. Mid-training on the generated data further enhances performance in both simulation and real-world robot settings.
